# Code API-based GraphQL API for WooCommerce

The goal of this project is to implement the infrastructure for a GraphQL API for WooCommerce with the following premises:

* Code API-first approach: manually maintained code classes will be the authoritative code API, the GraphQL infrastructure will be automatically generated based on that.
* Queries and mutations are represended by PHP classes using the command pattern.
* Data types (input and output types, enumerations...) are represented by DTO-style PHP classes.
* Conventions will be used wherever possible (e.g. all the classes in the queries directory map to equivalent GraphQL queries by default).
* Configuration based on PHP 8 attributes will be used where conventions fall short.
* GraphQL infrastructure code will be generated by a script at package build time.

## Superfluous and missing stuff in the prior art

To keep in mind when reading and interpreting the previous documents:

- This project will be PHP 8.1+ only. Compatbility with PHP 7 is NOT required. So e.g. GraphQL enumeration types can be safely mapped to native PHP enums.
- **COMPLETELY DISREGARD** any reference to REST API endpoints generation. This project is **EXCLUSIVELY** about GraphQL.
- Security (authentication, authorization) was excluded for the sake of simplicity when presenting concepts. We'll need to ineregrate it now, preferably reusing the WordPress roles and capabilities API
- https://github.com/webonyx/graphql-php will be used as the underlying GraphQL engine.

## Project stages

This project will be divided in the following stages:

1. Code API specification. Come up with a complete specification of the code API: directory structure, conventions in place, available attributes and usage rules for these, how each GraphQL entity is represented in code.
2. Supporting code specification. We need an infrastructure build script that will NOT be included in the WooCommerce package, autogenerted infrastructure code that will be committed to source code (all in dedicated directories to avoid confussion), and fixed infrastructure code (e.g. to register the GraphQL quierying endpoint).
3. Build process specification. When and how will the GraphQL infrastructure be generated (at build time, but ideally only when needed) and what will it generate exactly.
4. Generating the actual code API for a selected part of WooCommerce, to be decided later.
